is one step of the seminar. It ends with a **Do it** task and one set of
questions. The full explanations, examples and exercises are in the notes.

## Key terms

{{< glossary ipconfig default-gateway ping-tool network-latency jitter packet-loss traceroute nslookup speed-test bandwidth >}}

## 20.1 The tools and your address

- **ipconfig:** IP address, **default gateway**, DNS server.
- **ping:** latency and loss. **tracert:** the routers on the way.
- **nslookup:** name → IP. **Speed test:** bandwidth.
- Windows: Command Prompt (`cmd`). Linux and macOS: Terminal.
- 169.254.x.x and no gateway: no address from the router.

![Five network tools.](images/tools.png){width=94%}

![ipconfig.](images/ipconfig.png){width=94%}

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Your address"}
Run `ipconfig` (or use Terminal Lab in the office). Write the IPv4 address
and the default gateway.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · The tools"}
Choose the tool.

::: {.match extra="Paint|Task Manager"}
shows the default gateway
:   ipconfig

shows latency and lost packets

shows the routers on the way
:   tracert

gives the IP of a name
:   nslookup
:::
:::

## 20.2 ping and tracert

- **ping:** `time=` is the latency; "Request timed out" is a lost packet;
  the summary gives loss and average.
- Big differences between the times: **jitter**.
- **tracert:** one line per router (hop). Where the time jumps and stays
  high, the delay starts.
- Ping the **gateway** first, then the **server**.

![ping.](images/ping.png){width=94%}

![tracert.](images/tracert.png){width=94%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
A slow gateway means the problem is in the room, not on the Internet.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · ping and tracert"}
Ping your gateway and `example.com`; run `tracert example.com`. Write the
averages, the loss and the biggest jump.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Read the output"}
Use Terminal Lab. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="the DNS|the switch"}
4 sent, 3 received: the loss?
:   25 %

The café: the gateway ping jumps 6–160 ms. Where is the problem?
:   the Wi-Fi in the café

Home in the evening: the jump is at hop 4. Where is the delay?
:   outside the home, on the route

The office: 22–26 ms, 0 % loss. For a race?
:   good
:::
:::

## 20.3 DNS, bandwidth and a diagnosis

- **nslookup** fails but ping to the IP works → a **DNS** problem.
- **Speed test:** download and upload in Mbit/s.
- **From near to far:** ipconfig → ping gateway → ping server IP →
  nslookup → speed test. The first "no" shows the problem.
- Good ping and no loss but low FPS: the **device**, not the network.

![A diagnosis from near to far.](images/diagnosis.png){width=94%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Not every stutter is the network.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Your network report"}
Write six lines: address type, gateway ping, server ping and loss, hops,
download speed, and one sentence: good for an online race?
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · The diagnosis"}
Choose the problem.

::: {.match extra="the monitor|the keyboard"}
ipconfig: 169.254.10.4, no gateway
:   no address from the router

nslookup times out, ping to the IP works
:   the DNS

1.2 Mbit/s while three people stream videos
:   too little bandwidth

24 ms, 0 % loss, 18 FPS in battles
:   the device is too slow
:::
:::

## Game challenge: Lag Detective {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

Six players write to Byte Bay: **no address**, **jumping pings** in a
café, **server not found**, **lag every evening**, a **full home
connection**, and **stutter in big battles**.

{{< sim file="sims/lag-detective.html" poster="sims/lag-detective.png" title="Lag Detective: read the tools, find the problem" kind="game" height="620" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · The inbox"}
Choose the first tool for each message.

::: {.match extra="Paint|restart the server"}
“I cannot connect at all.”
:   ipconfig

“The game lags in the café.”
:   ping the gateway

“Server not found!”
:   nslookup

“Lag only in the evening.”
:   tracert
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · Numbers (harder)"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="hop 1|0 %"}
tracert 2, 8, 12, 98, 104 ms: the delay starts at
:   hop 4

8 sent, 6 received: the loss
:   25 %

ping 20, 150, 30, 200 ms: the problem
:   high jitter

ping 22, 23, 22, 24 ms: the jitter
:   low
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- ipconfig shows the address and the gateway; 169.254.x.x means no address.
- ping shows latency, jitter and loss; ping the gateway first.
- tracert shows where on the route the delay starts.
- nslookup checks the DNS; a speed test checks the bandwidth.
- Diagnose from near to far, and remember that the device can be the
  problem.
